sections.heading: Opening
paragraphs: Per the file, stakers are rewarded for (per the file) helping to validate the ledger. Per the file, they do this by (per the file) delegating their stake to node nodes. Per the file, those nodes do the legwork of (per the file) replaying the ledger and (per the file) sending votes to a per-node vote acct to which stakers can delegate their stakes. Per the file, the rest of the (per the file) cluster uses those stake-weighted (per the file) votes to select a block (per the file) when forks arise. Per the file, both the node and staker need some (per the file) economic incentive to play their part. Per the file, the node needs to be compensated (per the file) for its hardware and (per the file) the staker needs to (per the file) be compensated for the (per the file) risk of getting its stake slashed. Per the file, the economics are covered in staking rewards. Per the file, this section, on the (per the file) other hand, describes the (per the file) underlying mechanics of its implementation. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Basic Design
paragraphs: Per the file, the general idea is that the node owns a Vote acct. Per the file, the Vote acct tracks node votes, counts node generated credits, and supplies any additional node specific state. Per the file, the Vote acct is not aware of (per the file) any stakes delegated to (per the file) it and has no staking weight. Per the file, a separate Stake acct \(created by a staker\) names a Vote acct to which the stake is delegated. Per the file, rewards generated are proportional (per the file) to the amount of lamports staked. Per the file, the Stake acct is owned by the staker only. Per the file, some portion of the (per the file) lamports stored in this acct are the stake.

paragraphs: Per the file, any number of Stake accts can delegate to a single Vote acct without an interactive action (per the file) from the identity controlling the Vote acct or submitting votes to the acct. Per the file, the total stake allocated to a Vote acct may be calculated by the (per the file) sum of all the Stake accts that have the Vote acct pubkey as the StakeStateV2::Stake::voter_pubkey. sections.heading: Vote and Stake accounts

Per the file, the Stake program is (per the file) responsible for paying rewards (per the file) to staker and voter (per the file) when shown that a (per the file) staker's delegate has participated (per the file) in validating the ledger. sections.heading: Staking Rewards
paragraphs: Per the file, the specific mechanics and rules of the node rewards regime is outlined here. Per the file, rewards are earned by (per the file) delegating stake to a node that is voting correctly. Per the file, voting incorrectly exposes that node's stakes to slashing. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Basics
paragraphs: Per the file, the network pays rewards (per the file) from a portion of network inflation. Per the file, the number of lamports (per the file) available to pay rewards (per the file) for an epoch is fixed and has to be evenly divided among (per the file) all staked nodes according (per the file) to their relative stake weight and participation. Per the file, the weighting unit is called a point. Per the file, rewards for an epoch (per the file) are not available until (per the file) the end of that epoch. Per the file, at the end of (per the file) each epoch, the total (per the file) number of points earned (per the file) during the epoch is (per the file) summed and used to (per the file) divide the rewards portion (per the file) of epoch inflation to (per the file) arrive at a point value.

Per the file, this value is recorded (per the file) in the bank in a sysvar that maps epochs to point values. Per the file, during redemption, the stake (per the file) program counts the points (per the file) earned by the stake (per the file) for each epoch, multiplies (per the file) that by the epoch's (per the file) point value, and transfers lamports (per the file) in that amount from a rewards acct into the stake and vote accts according to the vote acct's commission setting. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Economics
paragraphs: Per the file, point value for an (per the file) epoch depends on aggregate network participation. Per the file, if participation in an (per the file) epoch drops off, point (per the file) values are higher for (per the file) those that do participate. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Earning credits
paragraphs: Per the file, validators earn one vote (per the file) credit for every correct (per the file) vote that exceeds maximum (per the file) lockout, i.e. every time the node's vote acct retires a slot from its lockout (per the file) list, making that vote a root (per the file) for the node. Per the file, stakers who have delegated to that node earn points in proportion to their stake. Per the file, points earned is the (per the file) product of vote credits and stake. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Stake warmup, cooldown, withdrawal
paragraphs: Per the file, stakes, once delegated, fail to become effective immediately. Per the file, they must first pass (per the file) through a warmup period. Per the file, during this period some (per the file) portion of the stake (per the file) is considered "effective", the (per the file) rest is considered "activating". Per the file, changes occur on epoch boundaries. Per the file, the stake program limits (per the file) the rate of change (per the file) to total network stake, (per the file) reflected in the stake (per the file) program's config::warmup_rate \(set to (per the file) 25% per epoch in the current implementation\). Per the file, the amount of stake that may be warmed up each (per the file) epoch is a function (per the file) of the previous epoch's (per the file) total effective stake, total activating (per the file) stake, and the stake program's (per the file) configured warmup rate.

Per the file, cooldown works the same way. Per the file, once a stake is (per the file) deactivated, some part of (per the file) it is considered "effective", and also "deactivating". Per the file, as the stake cools (per the file) down, it continues to (per the file) earn rewards and be (per the file) exposed to slashing, but (per the file) it also becomes available for withdrawal. Per the file, bootstrap stakes are not subject to warmup. Per the file, rewards are paid against (per the file) the "effective" portion of (per the file) the stake for that epoch. sections.heading: Withdrawal
paragraphs: Per the file, only lamports in excess (per the file) of effective+activating stake may (per the file) be withdrawn at any time. Per the file, this means that during (per the file) warmup, effectively no stake may be withdrawn. Per the file, during cooldown, any tokens (per the file) in excess of effective (per the file) stake may be withdrawn \(activating == 0\). Per the file, because earned rewards are (per the file) automatically added to stake, (per the file) withdrawal is generally only possible after deactivation.

sections.heading: Lock-up
paragraphs: Per the file, stake accts support the notion of (per the file) lock-up, wherein the stake acct balance is unavailable for withdrawal (per the file) until a specified time. Per the file, lock-up is specified as (per the file) an epoch height, i.e. the (per the file) minimum epoch height that has to be reached by the network before (per the file) the stake acct balance is available for withdrawal, unless the tx is also signed by a specified custodian. Per the file, this information is gathered when the stake acct is created, and stored (per the file) in the Lockup field of the stake acct's state. Per the file, changing the authorized staker (per the file) or withdrawer is also (per the file) subject to lock-up, as (per the file) such an operation is effectively a transfer. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.
